_meta: DRAFT — NOT YET IMPORTED into src/data/index.ts. Lead-chasing follow-up round after AF/G.22 (Sudan was covered at G.22, not G.23), 2026-08-13. Transcribes two new National Audit Chamber documents found via the same World Bank document-server mirror pattern that surfaced sd-nac-secrp-audit-2021, plus re-confirmation that audit.gov.sd remains unreachable and an inconclusive Wayback Machine retry. No new web research performed by this synthesis pass beyond transcribing the findings handed off.

reports.title: Audit Opinion — Sustainable Livelihood for Displaced & Vulnerable Communities in Eastern Sudan Project (SLDP), Agreement No. TFOAO3002, Financial Statements as at April 30, 2021
reports.publisher: National Audit Chamber (ديوان المراجعة القومي), Republic of the Sudan
reports.description: Sudan's National Audit Chamber's audit opinion on the World Bank-financed Sustainable Livelihood for Displaced & Vulnerable Communities in Eastern Sudan Project (SLDP), Agreement No. TFOAO3002. Opinion: "In our opinion, the financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the project as at April 30, 2021..." Auditing standard stated: "We conducted our audit in accordance with International Standards on Auditing (ISAs)." Follow-up instruction to the implementing agency: "It is also imperative that you carefully consider and follow-up the audit findings and Observations and ensure implementation of the audit recommendations." The project's geography names Khartoum and Kassala State — states not named in this branch's existing sd-nac-secrp-audit-2021 node (which names Central Darfur, North Darfur, and West Darfur, plus Blue Nile/Umm Kadada and Baw localities), so this is genuinely new sub-national coverage rather than a duplicate. Like sd-nac-secrp-audit-2021, this is an instance of this branch's richest evidence type: a higher-tier (federal/national) government body issuing a formal opinion that names and reports on specific lower-tier geographic units. NOTE ON HOSTING: hosted on the World Bank's project-document server (documents1.worldbank.org) as Bank-financed-grant disclosure, not on a Sudanese government domain (audit.gov.sd remains unreachable — see _dropped below) — but the content is Sudan-government-authored (National Audit Chamber letterhead and opinion), not World Bank-authored, so per this project's evidence rule it is treated as a primary Sudanese government source with the hosting caveat flagged explicitly, exactly as sd-nac-secrp-audit-2021 is. NOTE ON SCOPE: a project-specific grant audit opinion, not a general state/locality budget document — strong evidence of the Audit Chamber's practice of naming sub-national geography, but not a full state or locality finance publication.
reports.cadence_note: Project-specific audit opinion tied to a single World Bank grant's implementation period (financial statements as at April 30, 2021); not a recurring annual publication in the way a national budget is.

reports.title: Audit Opinion — Social Safety Net Project (SSNP), Grant Agreement No. 0A0362, Project ID P148349, Financial Statements as at December 31, 2020
reports.publisher: National Audit Chamber (ديوان المراجعة القومي), Republic of the Sudan
reports.description: Sudan's National Audit Chamber's audit opinion, on letterhead "Republic of the Sudan National Audit Chamber, P.O Box: 91 Khartoum," on the World Bank-financed Social Safety Net Project (SSNP), Grant Agreement No. 0A0362, Project ID P148349. Opinion: "In our opinion, the accompanying financial statements present fairly, in all material respects, the financial position of the project as at December 31, 2020." Follow-up instruction to the implementing agency: "It is also imperative that you carefully consider and follow-up the audit findings and Observations and ensure implementation of the audit recommendations." The project's geography names Khartoum, River Nile, Kassala, and North Kordofan states — broader state coverage than either sd-nac-secrp-audit-2021 (Central Darfur, North Darfur, West Darfur) or sd-nac-sldp-audit-2021 (Khartoum, Kassala) in this corpus, and again genuinely new sub-national coverage rather than a duplicate. Like the other two Audit Chamber nodes, this is an instance of this branch's richest evidence type: a higher-tier (federal/national) government body naming and reporting on specific lower-tier geographic units. NOTE ON HOSTING: hosted on the World Bank's project-document server (documents1.worldbank.org, .txt extraction of the PDF) as Bank-financed-grant disclosure, not on a Sudanese government domain (audit.gov.sd remains unreachable — see _dropped below) — but the content is Sudan-government-authored (National Audit Chamber letterhead and opinion), not World Bank-authored, so per this project's evidence rule it is treated as a primary Sudanese government source with the hosting caveat flagged explicitly, exactly as sd-nac-secrp-audit-2021 is. NOTE ON SCOPE: a project-specific grant audit opinion, not a general state/locality budget document — strong evidence of the Audit Chamber's practice of naming sub-national geography, but not a full state or locality finance publication. NOTE ON SOURCE FORMAT: the located copy is a .txt extraction (not a PDF render), so the exact submission month within the 2020 fiscal year is not fully legible in the extracted text; the fiscal-year-end date itself (December 31, 2020) is clear and quoted verbatim above.
reports.cadence_note: Project-specific audit opinion tied to a single World Bank grant's implementation period (financial statements as at December 31, 2020); not a recurring annual publication in the way a national budget is.

_dropped.why: All three National Audit Chamber nodes now in this branch (sd-nac-secrp-audit-2021, sd-nac-sldp-audit-2021, sd-nac-ssnp-audit-2020) are outputs of the same institution using the same stated audit methodology (each opinion invokes International Standards on Auditing, ISAs) and the same follow-up boilerplate instructing the implementing agency to act on findings. This is institutional/topical similarity, not a citable dependency: none of the three documents cross-references either of the other two by name, project ID, or agreement number, so no uses_data_from or cites edge is drawn between them per the evidence rule. Recorded here as a note rather than left undocumented, so a future round does not re-propose the same tempting-but-unsourced edge without checking first whether a later-located version of any of the three documents does contain an actual cross-reference (e.g. a consolidated Audit Chamber annual report citing individual project audits by name).

RE-CONFIRMED this round, now a twice-confirmed, stable finding (first found AF/G.22): Sudan's National Audit Chamber's own domain (audit.gov.sd) is still unreachable by DNS resolution failure. Given that the underlying cause (wartime infrastructure disruption since the 2023 civil war) is structural rather than transient, and the finding has now been independently reproduced twice with the same failure mode, this is not expected to change on any short timescale — a future round should NOT spend research effort re-checking audit.gov.sd again in the near term (e.g. within the next several rounds) unless there is specific news of Sudanese government infrastructure/connectivity being restored, or of the war's status changing materially. A periodic re-check (e.g. once every several months of project time, or triggered by broader Sudan-infrastructure news) is still worthwhile precisely because of the wartime context — government sites do occasionally come back online abruptly — but treating this as an open action item for every round is not a good use of research effort. All three Audit Chamber nodes in this corpus (sd-nac-secrp-audit-2021, sd-nac-sldp-audit-2021, sd-nac-ssnp-audit-2020) continue to be sourced only via the World Bank's document-mirror/disclosure copies, not the Chamber's own site.

_dropped.edge: sd-audit-chamber own-domain publications -> Wayback Machine archive
_dropped.why: GENUINELY UNRESOLVED, not a confirmed absence of any archive: this round retried the Wayback Machine for audit.gov.sd (following up on AF/G.22's single 429 attempt) across multiple spaced attempts and every one returned HTTP 429 Too Many Requests; alternate access paths (the CDX API and the calendar/timemap view) were also tried and returned an HTTP 403 that appears to originate from the proxy layer rather than from archive.org itself. Because every attempt failed at the transport/rate-limit layer rather than returning a substantive 'no captures found' response, this does NOT establish that audit.gov.sd has no Wayback Machine history — it only establishes that this round could not get a conclusive answer either way. A future round should retry with wider spacing between attempts (and, if possible, from a path that avoids the proxy's CDX/calendar-view block) before concluding either that an archived copy exists or that none does.
